title: wkharness agent bulletin (shared live steering channel for background agents)
desc: Design for a shared append-only bulletin file that all running background agents reference live, force-fed by a PostToolUse hook (per-agent seq cursor plus @all and @agent addressing). Live counterpart to CLAUDE.md; fills the Bash-launched Agent.cmd background-agent gap that SendMessage does not cover. Enables mid-run persistence nudges, broadcast stop or constraint, clean abort, and inter-agent coordination. STATUS 2026-05-29: PLANNED.
steps: Problem: Bash-launched Agent.cmd background agents have no live steering channel. The IDE Agent tool has SendMessage, but the wkcodex and Agent.cmd background path does not, so you cannot course-correct or send persistence nudges mid-run; only kill and restart, which wastes partial progress and tokens.

Solution: one shared append-only bulletin file (a blackboard or event log) that every running agent references live. A single append reaches all agents at once, and agents can also leave notes for each other.

Delivery is harness-enforced, not model-polled. A PostToolUse hook on each subagent tails the bulletin and injects unconsumed relevant lines into the agent next turn, prefixed BULLETIN. Cheap models forget to poll, so the hook force-feeds them.
Per-reader cursor: one file, N cursors. The injector stores each agent last-seen seq number in a sidecar json keyed by agent-id, so each agent receives only lines newer than what it already consumed.

Addressing: each line carries a target token. at-all broadcasts to every agent; at-agent-ID targets one. The injector keeps a line when the target matches this agent AND the seq is newer than the agent cursor.

Append-only and atomic: writers only append, never rewrite. Each line is seq plus timestamp plus target plus message. This avoids interleave corruption when several writers (orchestrator and agents) append concurrently.
Size cap and rotation: cap the bulletin and drop fully-consumed old lines so per-turn re-scan does not bloat tokens. Cursors survive rotation because they track seq, not byte offset.

Use cases: orchestrator persistence nudges (do not give up, work the next fallback rung), broadcast stop or a new constraint, clean abort when work moved elsewhere, and inter-agent handoff notes. Live counterpart to CLAUDE.md, which is the static shared file read once at session start.

Build phases: P0 single shared file plus manual append plus injector hook with one global cursor for broadcast only. P1 per-agent seq cursor sidecar. P2 addressing for at-all and at-agent-ID. P3 rotation and size cap. P4 a wk helper command to append a bulletin line plus self-test cases.

Relation to existing infra: builds on the wkharness PostToolUse hook. SendMessage already covers in-harness Agent-tool agents; this skill fills the Bash-launched Agent.cmd background-agent gap. STATUS 2026-05-29 PLANNED, enshrined per user request, not yet built.
